scenes.text: How does an animated film go from an idea to the big screen? It moves through a pipeline.
It starts with storyboards. Artists sketch the film shot by shot, then cut the sketches into a story reel with temporary voices.
Layout sets the camera. Simple stand-in models block out each shot, and artists choose the angles and camera moves.
Then animators bring the characters to life, pose by pose, at twenty-four frames for every second of film.
Lighting sets the mood. Virtual lights are placed like on a real film set, and colour guides where you look.
Finally every frame is rendered as a finished image. A ninety-minute film needs almost one hundred and thirty thousand of them.
